data.narrative:
Infleqtion, a public-stage quantum computing company founded by Dana Anderson, has raised $760M+ and currently trades at a $1.92B valuation. The quantum computing sector comprises three public comparables (IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing) and eight additional private peers including Quantinuum and IQM Quantum Computers.

Peer-median valuation represents the applicable triangulation method. The three public-stage quantum computing comparables trade at a median valuation of $6.3B, with a range spanning $4.5B (Rigetti Computing) to $13.0B (IonQ). This method yields an implied valuation of $6.3B for Infleqtion based on sector and stage alignment.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $5.3B (low) to $7.2B (high), with a median of $6.3B. Infleqtion's current $1.92B trading valuation sits substantially below this peer-derived range, reflecting a discount of approximately 70% relative to the median comparable. Key uncertainties include the stability of quantum computing peer multiples given sector maturity and commercialization timelines, as well as Infleqtion-specific competitive positioning relative to the broader peer set. The single-method triangulation narrows conviction; additional approaches (revenue multiples, DCF-based frameworks) would strengthen analytical support.
